correctness.rationale: The smaller degree-three cell H is independent; the degree-two cell L induces a perfect matching, and cross-edge counting gives |L|=3|H| with |H| positive and even. Each matched pair gives either a triangle at one center or a three-edge path between centers. In the contracted multigraph on H, deleting loops leaves a connected graph. Any cycle, including two parallel edges, lifts to an induced cycle of length at least six since H is independent and interior vertices have degree two. Hence the loopless graph is a simple tree. The equation deg_T(v)+2m_v=3 gives degrees one and three with triangles precisely at leaves. The converse has only bridge and triangle blocks. The degree-three core and the unique K2 base case give the inverse; the tree handshake gives the counts. Uniform color refinement splits by degree and stabilizes, and counting distinguishes different total orders. The first two core types at k=4 and the fixed-total-length spider family prove the threshold and unbounded multiplicity. An independent enumeration of the minimal off-loop edge strata and the labeled four-vertex core confirms the small profiles (python3 /workspace/review-evidence/check_frozen.py, chordal); it is not the infinite proof.
